findings.title: Async legacy write uses request-derived context that is likely canceled before the goroutine runs
findings.body: In Create (and similarly in Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) the goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)` where the outer `ctx` is the context passed into the handler, derived from the original request context. Once the HTTP handler returns (which happens right after this goroutine is spawned, since Create/Update/Delete return immediately), the apiserver typically cancels the request context. Because the goroutine's context is a child of that same request context, it will be cancelled almost immediately, well before the intended 10s timeout, causing `d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection` to fail with 'context canceled' on virtually every call. This defeats the entire purpose of Mode 3 (writing to legacy asynchronously 'as a safe measure'), since the legacy write will essentially never complete successfully. The context used in the goroutine should be detached from request cancellation (e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` combined with the timeout, or a fresh background context carrying only the relevant values).

findings.title: Storage Create error incorrectly recorded as a legacy-duration metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. This mislabels a unified-storage failure as a legacy-storage failure in metrics, corrupting the dual-writer observability data used to monitor Mode 3 health. The same pattern recurs in Update's error branch (line 129).

findings.title: Storage Update error incorrectly recorded via recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: On the error path after `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, mislabeling a unified-storage error as a legacy error. This should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`, consistent with the Delete and DeleteCollection error paths.

findings.title: Metric label uses object name instead of resource kind, risking unbounded metric cardinality
findings.body: In Delete, the success path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`, passing the deleted object's `name` where every other call site (and the metric's label semantics) expects `options.Kind`. Besides being inconsistent, feeding a per-object name into a metric label can create unbounded cardinality in Prometheus (a new label value per deleted object), which can bloat metric storage and cause performance/memory issues on the metrics backend.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection error recorded through recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: In the async goroutine in DeleteCollection, after calling `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. Since this measures the Legacy store call, it should use `d.recordLegacyDuration`, not `d.recordStorageDuration`. This causes legacy failures/timings to be misattributed to storage in metrics.

findings.title: Async legacy writes silently drop error details, losing observability on failures
findings.body: The previous (synchronous) implementation logged errors from the Legacy store calls (e.g. `log.Error(errLS, "could not delete from legacy store")`). The new async goroutines in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection only record a boolean into a duration metric and never log the actual error returned by the Legacy store call. Since these goroutines are fire-and-forget with no caller visibility, failing legacy writes become effectively invisible except through aggregate metrics, making it hard to diagnose data drift between the legacy store and unified storage.

findings.title: Delete uses d.Log instead of the request-scoped logger with additional context fields
findings.body: In Delete, `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` is created, but then `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` stores `d.Log` (without the added name/kind/method values) into the context instead of the local `log` variable. This means any logger retrieved from the context downstream loses the name/kind/method fields that were just added, unlike the Create, Get, List, Update, and DeleteCollection methods which correctly propagate their local `log` variable.

findings.title: Tests do not wait for the async legacy goroutine before asserting, making legacy-write verification unreliable
findings.body: TestMode3_Create (and the Delete/Update/DeleteCollection tests) set up mock expectations on the shared `mock.Mock` for the Legacy store call, but `DualWriterMode3.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection` fire the legacy write in a goroutine and return immediately. The tests assert results and move on without any synchronization (e.g. a WaitGroup or channel) to ensure the goroutine has completed. This means the tests don't actually verify the legacy write happened, and since the same `mock.Mock` instance (`m`) can continue to be accessed by a lingering goroutine after the subtest finishes, running tests with `-race` can surface data races, and leftover goroutines can interact with mocks from a subsequent subtest case.

findings.title: Duplicate go.work.sum entry introduced
findings.body: The diff re-adds `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod h1:DkxMin+qOh1Fgkxfbt+CUfBqqsCQJMG9op8Os/irBPA=` as a new line even though an identical line already exists immediately above (unchanged context). This creates a duplicate checksum entry, which is a symptom of an unclean dependency sync/rebase and should be cleaned up (e.g. by re-running `go work sync`/`go mod tidy`) rather than merged in with a duplicate line.
